title: drill, explaining itself
note: The sample pack. Everything in it is about the tool you are holding.

sections.title: What this tool is
sections.html:
drill is a study machine with no material in it. It holds no questions and no reference text of its own: you load a content pack from your own device, it is read by this page, and it stays on the device it was loaded on.

Nothing is uploaded. There is no server to send it to.

That is the design rather than a limitation. Material somebody else owns can be studied without ever being published: the machine is published, the material is yours. It also makes the permission conversation a short one - you can show somebody the machine running, empty, and say “your material drops in as a pack”.

This pack is the exception that proves it. Everything in it is about the tool you are holding, which is the one subject where a wrong answer cannot mislead anybody about the sea.

sections.title: The pack
sections.html:
A pack is one JSON file named *.drillpack.json. It is read by the page, validated whole, and kept in this browser's own database. Loading a pack replaces the one held.

Required: format, which must begin bashnav-drill-pack/; a non-empty sections; a non-empty questions.

Optional: title, note, built, pass and back. Set built: without it a rebuilt pack is indistinguishable from the one it replaced, and a question you were sure you had fixed comes round again.

A section needs an id, unique in the pack, and a title. Its html is the reference text, and the reference is the part that is always open.

A pack is rejected whole: loading half of one would give a drill with silent holes in it.

sections.title: Questions
sections.html:
A question names its section and carries its prompt in q.

The presence of a is what makes a question graded. With an answer, it can be marked. Without one it is a recall prompt: you are asked, you think, and you check yourself against the reference. Recall prompts are asked first in a practice run, because they are the harder kind.

ch holds wrong options to offer beside the answer. None may equal the answer and none may repeat - a wrong option that equals the answer is a question with two right answers, and the mark it gives is a lie either way.

seq and extra make an ordering question: three or more steps in their right order, and at least one step that does not belong. No step may appear in both.

where is the citation shown under the question - part, sub, row - so an answer can be traced back to the material. kind: "hand" marks a question written by hand, and it is labelled as such when asked.

sections.title: Sections, progress and the reference
sections.html:
The first section is open from the start. Each later one opens when the one before it is passed, at the pack's own pass mark, or 80 per cent if the pack does not say.

The reference is never locked, including for sections you have not reached. Being locked out of a procedure you are carrying this for is the one failure that would matter.

Studied means worked, not opened. Reading the reference does not count as studying a section; a recall prompt marked or a test taken does.

Progress is kept per section id, in this browser, on this device. A rebuilt pack that keeps its ids keeps your progress.

questions.q: Where does a pack you load go?
questions.a: Nowhere. It is read by this page and kept on this device.
ch: To the server that published drill, so it can be shared
Into the tool's own published files
To whoever wrote the pack, as a usage report

questions.a: The machine is published. The material is yours and stays yours.
ch: Both are published together
Neither: the tool is private to the person who built it
The material is published and the machine is licensed

questions.a: format, sections and questions.
ch: title, sections and questions
format, title and built
format, sections and pass

It loads, and the bad questions are hidden
It loads in a read-only mode

questions.q: Why is 'built' worth setting even though it is optional?
questions.a: Without it a rebuilt pack looks exactly like the one it replaced.
ch: It is what unlocks the first section
The tool refuses a pack older than thirty days
It sets the pass mark

questions.q: What makes a question graded rather than a recall prompt?
questions.a: It has an answer in 'a'.
ch: It has wrong options in 'ch'
It is marked kind: graded
It belongs to a section that has been passed

questions.q: Which of these is refused?
questions.a: A wrong option that is the same text as the answer.
ch: A question with no wrong options at all
A question whose answer is longer than its prompt
Two questions in the same section with the same prompt

An ordering question needs what, besides the steps in their right order?
questions.a: At least one step that does not belong, in 'extra'.
ch: A time limit
An answer in 'a' as well
At least five steps

questions.q: When does the second section open?
questions.a: When the first is passed.
ch: As soon as the pack is loaded
When the first has been read
When every question in the first has been seen once

questions.q: A pack says nothing about a pass mark. What is it?
questions.a: 80 per cent.
ch: 50 per cent
100 per cent
There is none: every section is open

questions.a: The reference. It is never locked.
ch: None of it
The questions, but not their answers
The first question only

questions.a: It replaces it.

questions.a: In this browser's own database, on this device.

In the file you loaded it from, which is read each time

questions.q: A section has an id, a title and what else, optionally?
questions.a: html, which is its reference text.
ch: questions, listed inside the section
pass, its own mark
parts, which name its subsections

questions.a: A recall prompt. Without an answer it is never graded, whatever else it carries.
ch: An ordering question in the test
Invalid, and the pack is refused
A graded question marked on the order alone

questions.a: It marks a question written by hand, and the question says so when it is asked.
ch: It makes the question appear first
It excludes the question from the test
It tells the tool to accept a typed answer

questions.a: It is kept: progress is held per section id.
ch: It is cleared, because the pack is replaced
It is kept only for sections whose questions did not change
It is merged, and the better of the two scores is kept

questions.a: In this browser, on this device. Clearing site data clears it.
ch: In the pack file, which is written back
With the pack's author
In the tool's published files

questions.a: It stays yours, on your device.
ch: It is published with the tool

back: That is the whole of the machine. What goes in it is yours.
